short_description: A seated core exercise that draws the knees in and extends the legs out to work the abs and hip flexors.
how_to: Sit on the floor with your hands behind you for support.
Lean back slightly and lift your feet off the floor.
Draw your knees in toward your chest.
Extend both legs back out straight.
Repeat at a steady pace, keeping your feet from touching the floor.
correct: Keep your core engaged throughout.
Keep your back straight, not hunched.
Control the extension rather than kicking out.
Breathe steadily with each rep.
mistakes: Don't let your feet rest on the floor between reps.
Don't round your back heavily.
Don't use your arms to push yourself through the movement.
Don't hold your breath.

short_description: A supine core exercise that curls the hips up toward the chest to target the lower abs.
how_to: Lie on your back with your hands flat beside you for support.
Bend your knees and lift your feet off the floor.
Draw your knees toward your chest by curling your hips up.
Lower your hips back down with control.
Repeat without letting your feet touch the floor.
correct: Keep your lower back controlled against the floor.
Keep the movement slow and deliberate.
Curl your hips, not just your knees.
Breathe out as you draw your knees in.
mistakes: Don't arch your lower back.
Don't pull on your neck.
Don't swing your legs to generate momentum.
Don't let your hips crash back down.

short_description: A dynamic plank variation that drives the knee across to the opposite elbow to engage the core and obliques.
how_to: Start in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders.
Brace your core and keep your hips level.
Drive your right knee diagonally toward your left elbow.
Return your foot to the start and repeat on the other side.
Alternate sides at a controlled pace.
correct: Keep your body in one line between reps.
Keep your core engaged at all times.
Keep your hips from rotating as you drive the knee.
Breathe steadily throughout.
mistakes: Don't let your lower back sag.
Don't lift your hips too high.
Don't rush the movement and lose hip control.
Don't hold your breath.

short_description: A seated dumbbell exercise that tucks the knees in while holding weights to load the core and hip flexors.
how_to: Sit on the floor holding a dumbbell at your chest with both hands.
Lean back slightly and lift your feet off the floor.
Draw your knees in toward your chest.
Extend your legs back out while maintaining your lean.
Repeat without letting your feet rest on the floor.
correct: Keep your core tight throughout the movement.
Keep your back straight rather than rounded.
Hold the dumbbell steady against your chest.
Breathe out as you tuck your knees in.
mistakes: Don't let your feet touch the floor between reps.
Don't round your back excessively.
Don't use the dumbbell's weight as a counterbalance.
Don't hold your breath.

short_description: A seated core exercise that traces slow circles with the torso to strengthen the obliques and deep abdominals.
how_to: Sit upright with your knees bent and feet flat or raised slightly.
Clasp your hands in front of you or cross them over your chest.
Lean back slightly to engage your core.
Slowly trace a large circle with your upper body.
Complete the desired reps in each direction.
correct: Keep your core engaged throughout the full circle.
Move slowly and deliberately in each direction.
Keep your back flat rather than heavily rounded.
Breathe steadily as you circle.
mistakes: Don't rush through the circles.
Don't collapse forward and lose your core tension.
Don't hold your breath.
Don't anchor your movement only at the shoulders.

short_description: A supine glute exercise that presses the hips up to strengthen the glutes and hamstrings.
how_to: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Place your arms flat at your sides.
Press through your heels and lift your hips toward the ceiling.
Squeeze your glutes at the top.
Lower your hips back down with control and repeat.
correct: Keep your feet flat and hip-width apart.
Squeeze your glutes fully at the top position.
Keep your knees pointing forward, not falling outward.
Breathe out as you press up.
mistakes: Don't push your hips so high that your back arches excessively.
Don't let your knees fall outward.
Don't drop your hips without control.
Don't hold your breath at the top.

short_description: A standing dumbbell exercise that bends the torso sideways to work the obliques.
how_to: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, holding a dumbbell in one hand.
Place your free hand behind your head or on your hip.
Keep your back straight and slowly bend sideways toward the dumbbell.
Return to upright by contracting the opposite oblique.
Complete the desired reps and switch sides.
correct: Keep your back straight throughout the movement.
Move directly to the side, not forward or back.
Control the return to upright rather than snapping back.
Keep your shoulders level.
mistakes: Don't lean forward or backward as you bend.
Don't use a heavy swing to move the weight.
Don't shrug your shoulder on the working side.
Don't hold your breath.

short_description: A lateral crunch that targets the obliques by curling the torso sideways.
how_to: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat.
Place both hands behind your head.
Curl your right shoulder toward your right hip.
Lower back with control and repeat on the same side.
Switch sides after the desired reps.
correct: Keep your lower back controlled against the floor.
Keep your elbows wide, not pulled forward.
Focus the movement on the side of your waist.
Breathe out on each crunch.
mistakes: Don't arch your lower back.
Don't pull on your neck.
Don't rotate excessively — keep the motion lateral.
Don't use momentum to reach higher.

short_description: A crunch performed with legs raised vertically to increase lower-ab engagement.
how_to: Lie on your back and raise both legs straight up to vertical.
Place your hands behind your head.
Curl your shoulders off the floor toward your raised legs.
Lower your shoulders back down with control.
Repeat while keeping your legs vertical throughout.
correct: Keep your lower back controlled against the floor.
Keep your legs as straight as possible.
Keep your chin slightly tucked, not forced to your chest.
Breathe out on each crunch.
mistakes: Don't arch your lower back.
Don't pull on your neck.
Don't let your legs drift away from vertical.
Don't hold your breath.

short_description: A rotating plank that lifts one arm to the ceiling, challenging core stability and shoulder strength.
how_to: Begin in a high plank with your hands under your shoulders.
Shift your weight to your right hand.
Rotate your body open and lift your left arm straight toward the ceiling.
Hold for a moment, then return to plank.
Repeat on the other side, alternating each rep.
correct: Keep your body in one line during the rotation.
Keep your core engaged so your hips don't drop.
Stack your feet or stagger them for balance.
Breathe steadily through each rotation.
mistakes: Don't let your lower back sag.
Don't lift your hips too high.
Don't rush the rotation and lose control.
Don't hold your breath.
